after: Tuesday comes straight after Monday each week.
Can we have pudding after our dinner?
After the rain stopped, we splashed in puddles.
fast: The little red car goes very fast.
Why is the toy train so fast today?
A snail that is fast would be a surprise!
last: December is the last month of the year.
This is the last page of my book.
Who ate the last biscuit in the tin?
past: Yesterday is part of the past, but tomorrow is not.
Are knights and castles part of the past?
Dinosaurs lived in the past, before any people.
father: My father drove us to the seaside.
I gave my father a card for his birthday.
Is that tall man your father?
class: Our teacher read the whole class a story.
Which class are you in this year?
We painted a big picture as a class.
grass: The sheep are eating the fresh grass.
Is the grass wet with morning dew?
A ladybird sat on a blade of grass!
sky: The moon and stars shine in the sky tonight.
The sun sets and the sky turns orange!
Rain falls from a dark sky.
fly: I wish I could fly like a bird!
Bees buzz and fly from flower to flower.
We will fly in a plane on holiday.
babies: Little babies drink milk from bottles.
Babies learn to crawl before they walk.
Look at those tiny babies waving their hands!

rejected.s: Wash your hands after painting with messy glue.
rejected.reason: checker: Painting with glue is an odd idea that may confuse a young reader.

rejected.s: Run fast to catch the bus!
rejected.reason: checker: Running for a bus suggests hurrying near a road, which is not safe play.

rejected.s: Hold on tight, the roundabout is spinning fast!
rejected.reason: checker: Holding on tight to a fast-spinning ride hints at danger, and roundabout could also mean a road junction.

rejected.s: Z is the last letter of the alphabet.
rejected.reason: machine rule 4: not on the word lists: Z

rejected.s: Hooray, we sang the last song of the show!
rejected.reason: checker: The fast song of the show makes sense too, so the gap is ambiguous. (also fits: fast)

rejected.s: Grandad likes to tell stories about the past.
rejected.reason: machine rule 4: not on the word lists: Grandad

rejected.s: Old photos tell us about the past.
rejected.reason: checker: Old photos could tell us about the class or the babies too. (also fits: class, babies)

rejected.s: The train zoomed past me without stopping.
rejected.reason: checker: Here past is a preposition, not the time before now, and after could also go in the gap. (also fits: after)

rejected.s: My mum and father both love the park.
rejected.reason: checker: Mum and father is an unnatural pair; people would say mum and dad.

rejected.s: Dad is another name for a father.
rejected.reason: checker: This just repeats the meaning instead of using the word in a real situation.

rejected.s: Look up! The sky is full of grey clouds.
rejected.reason: machine rule 2,4: more than one sentence; capital word not allowed: The

rejected.s: Which babies are wearing the yellow hats?
rejected.reason: checker: Which class are wearing the yellow hats also works in British English. (also fits: class)

rejected.s: Our museum visit showed us life in the past.
rejected.reason: checker: A museum could also show life in the grass or in the sky, so a child might pick the wrong word. (also fits: grass, sky)
